correctness.rationale: The surface is defined as a compact Euclidean quotient with a convex universal covering strip, so the intrinsic distance equals the exact image minimum for every pair. Parity of the deck transformation reduces the minimum to two expressions; triangular horizontal-difference density and logarithmic transverse product density are derived and exactly integrated in each parameter branch. Symbolic differentiation confirms the matching first three but not fourth derivatives at A=1. Global uniqueness is established by the derivative sign of F and the unique root of h above A=3. Standard-library verification has passed 100000 image-pair checks, deterministic quadrature over ten parameters, 1020000 Monte Carlo pairs, and root checks. Finite experiments corroborate and do not replace exact proof.

value.rationale: Average squared intrinsic separation is a canonical metric-measure invariant of a compact nonorientable surface with boundary. The exact all-width formula, the analytically sharp fourth-derivative activation threshold, and the unique nontrivial fixed-area aspect-ratio minimum answer a natural geometric design question. Explicit comparison with the orientable cylinder distinguishes the two quotient topologies. Unlike arbitrary finite slices, the classification is for all continuous positive shapes, and the abstract-versus-embedded limitation is stated.
